per_plume.source_hint: marine cloud line advected WSW, no vent/fire connection
evidence: USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW not erupting (paused summit eruption) and Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, arguing against fresh vog supply. [E1]

Plume is detached and far from vents: centroid 84.9 km from Kilauea and 90.6 km from Mauna Loa, upwind end 81.8 km and 97.5 km respectively, and tracked source end over ocean NE of Hawaii at 20.305N 154.905W, 107.5 km from Kilauea and 118.0 km from Mauna Loa. [E3, E9, E4]
Wind at Kilauea summit from 38 deg (blowing toward 218 deg SW) would carry any summit emission southwest, inconsistent with a streak east/northeast of the island. [E8]

Measured drift toward 244 deg at 32 km/h with fit R2 0.98 agrees within ~23 deg of wind-implied transport toward 267 deg (wind from 87 deg at inferred source) to 281 deg (wind from 101 deg at centroid), supporting passive advection of a cloud line rather than vent-trailing vog, whose N-S 115-km elongation is cross-wind. [E2, E7, E4]

FIRMS shows no fire clusters in 19-21N 156-154.5W box to support smoke, and mask is 11.6% land over ocean only (2.8% Hawaii), consistent with a marine cloud streak rather than land-based fire; faint translucent gray narrow form distinct from bright white cumulus still fits thin cloud. [E6, E5]

evidence_cited.text: USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW not erupting (paused summit eruption) and Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, arguing against fresh vog supply.

Plume is detached and far from vents: centroid 84.9 km from Kilauea and 90.6 km from Mauna Loa, upwind end 81.8 km and 97.5 km respectively, and tracked source end over ocean NE of Hawaii at 20.305N 154.905W, 107.5 km from Kilauea and 118.0 km from Mauna Loa.
Wind at Kilauea summit from 38 deg (blowing toward 218 deg SW) would carry any summit emission southwest, inconsistent with a streak east/northeast of the island.

Measured drift toward 244 deg at 32 km/h with fit R2 0.98 agrees within ~23 deg of wind-implied transport toward 267 deg (wind from 87 deg at inferred source) to 281 deg (wind from 101 deg at centroid), supporting passive advection of a cloud line rather than vent-trailing vog, whose N-S 115-km elongation is cross-wind.

FIRMS shows no fire clusters in 19-21N 156-154.5W box to support smoke, and mask is 11.6% land over ocean only (2.8% Hawaii), consistent with a marine cloud streak rather than land-based fire; faint translucent gray narrow form distinct from bright white cumulus still fits thin cloud.

classify.caveats: Single faint narrow feature with no in-situ composition; thin remnant vog or dilute smoke cannot be fully excluded from true-color alone, but official non-erupting status, large vent distances and lack of fires weigh against vog/smoke.

kilauea.activity_summary: Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. After a period of instability, the summit has reinflated more steadily over the past two days. More data are needed to model the forecast window for the next episode.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in July, while the summit region showed patterns of slight inflation. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 57 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the July reporting period, after 94 in June. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
